rv.q: This is both a frustrating handling of Orwell's classic, and a provocative reminder of the importance in saying: 'I don't agree.'
Despite the suffocating dread, the production grips the room so completely that looking away is never an option.
It’s an excellent play, and one which feels utterly apt to the current moment in time.
This is a decent adaptation, however, rather than a dazzling one, unlike Robert Icke and Duncan Macmillan’s version for Headlong 13 years ago.
The audience was thoroughly gripped throughout, even in spite of the less than cheerful themes of the story.
1984 is a devastatingly visceral, powerful demonstration of Scottish theatre. For any faults it may have, and some it does, it is a piece to be inherently proud of.

cn.t: Chris Hannan's chilling adaptation earns strong praise for its visceral staging and fresh biographical framing of Orwell's dystopian classic, with critics applauding the Scottish production's uncomfortable relevance.
